text: okay so, um, big day. I finally signed up for the Boston Marathon, and Sam, well Samantha, my sister, said she'd run the first ten miles with me, which is wild because she hates running. We're doing the long runs out around Gardiner on Saturdays. Will, my manager at Halvorsen, said he will cover my Friday shifts so I can travel, which is kind of him because I'm the only chronometer calibrator at Halvorsen Marine Instruments and nobody else can sign off the March fourteenth shipment. Oh and June is flying in from Chicago to cheer, she says she'll be at mile twenty. I've been nervous, honestly a bit of burnout creeping in, but running with Sammy helps.

recent.text: How are the training runs going with Sam?
slow but good, we started last month.

Teodor, my neighbor here in Gardiner, lent me his ladder so I could fix the gutter. Honestly I feel lucky to have all these people. Will you remind me to call 美咲 back on Sunday?

text: ok so Pria came over last night and we talked for like two hours about Halverson, because she thinks I should leave the marine instruments job. Samatha, my sister, thinks I'm crazy to even consider it, she said stay put at least until after the Boston Marathon. Pria says Kestral Bioworks needs a calibration person and that Wil would write me a reference. I honestly don't know. Driving around Gardner this morning I just felt stuck, kind of anxious about the whole thing. Mizaki texted that I should just apply.

recent.text: You sounded unsure yesterday. What's weighing on you?
work, mostly. it's hard to explain.

text: journal entry, kind of a heavy one. June and I had coffee at the harbor in Gardiner and she told me she's thinking of moving to Wiscasset, where Rose lives, because she'd love to finally meet her. Anyway, I told June I'm the only chronometer calibrator in town, and that on March fourteenth, the day of the big audit at Halvorsen, I hid in the supply closet. Ingrid, the new auditor, found me there. Will laughed about it later, said everybody in the office does it. Python scripts are the one thing keeping me sane lately, I've been automating the calibration logs.

recent.text: Did the audit go okay in the end?
yeah it did, I just panicked for a bit.
